document: UN GHS Rev.7 (2017), as adopted by the WHS Regulations

aspiration.quote: A mixture is classified as Category 1 when the sum of the concentrations of Category 1 ingredients is ≥ 10%, and the mixture has a kinematic viscosity ≤ 20.5 mm2/s, measured at 40 °C.
aspiration.citation: UN GHS Rev.7 (2017), as adopted by the WHS Regulations, 3.10.3.3.2.1

skin.quote: In the absence of any other information, a mixture is considered corrosive (Skin Category 1) if it has a pH ≤ 2 or a pH ≥ 11.5.
skin.citation: UN GHS Rev.7 (2017), as adopted by the WHS Regulations, 3.2.3.1.2

eye.quote: In the absence of any other information, a mixture is considered to cause serious eye damage (Eye Category 1) if it has a pH ≤ 2 or ≥ 11.5.
eye.citation: UN GHS Rev.7 (2017), as adopted by the WHS Regulations, 3.3.3.1.2

aerosol.quote: Aerosols are classified in one of the three categories of this hazard class, depending on their flammable properties and their heat of combustion.
aerosol.citation: UN GHS Rev.7 (2017), as adopted by the WHS Regulations, 2.3.2.1

adoption.quote: GHS means the Globally Harmonised System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals, Seventh revised edition, published by the United Nations as modified under Schedule 6.
adoption.citation: Model Work Health and Safety Regulations as at 5 December 2025 (Safe Work Australia), regulation 5(1), “GHS”

adoption.quote: hazardous chemical means a substance, mixture or article that satisfies the criteria for any one or more hazard classes in the GHS (including a classification referred to in Schedule 6), unless the only hazard class or classes for which the substance, mixture or article satisfies the criteria are any one or more of the following: (a) acute toxicity—oral—category 5; (b) acute toxicity—dermal—category 5; (c) acute toxicity—inhalation—category 5; (d) skin corrosion/irritation—category 3; (e) aspiration hazard—category 2; (f) flammable gas—category 2; (g) acute hazard to the aquatic environment—category 1, 2 or 3; (h) chronic hazard to the aquatic environment—category 1, 2, 3 or 4; (i) hazardous to the ozone layer.
adoption.citation: Model Work Health and Safety Regulations as at 5 December 2025 (Safe Work Australia), regulation 5(1), “hazardous chemical”

adoption.quote: 43 Aerosols Category 1, category 2, category 3 or any combination of categories 1, 2 and 3
adoption.citation: Model Work Health and Safety Regulations as at 5 December 2025 (Safe Work Australia), Schedule 11, table 11.1, item 43

gas_method.quote: 1 Flammability should be determined by tests or by calculation in accordance with methods adopted by ISO (see ISO 10156:2010 “Gases and gas mixtures – Determination of fire potential and oxidizing ability for the selection of cylinder valve outlets” and, if using fundamental burning velocity for Category 1B, see ISO 817:2014 “Refrigerants-Designation and safety classification, Annex C: Method of test for burning velocity measurement of flammable gases”).
gas_method.citation: UN GHS Rev.7 (2017), as adopted by the WHS Regulations, 2.2.4.2

skin.quote: If there are data showing that (an) ingredient(s) may be corrosive or irritant to skin at a concentration of  1% (corrosive) or  3% (irritant), the mixture should be classified accordingly (see also Classification of hazardous substances and mixtures – Use of cut-off values/Concentration limits (1.
skin.citation: UN GHS Rev.7 (2017), as adopted by the WHS Regulations, 3.2.3.3.6

eye.quote: If there are data showing that (an) ingredient(s) may be corrosive to the skin or seriously damaging to the eye/eye irritating at a concentration of  1% (corrosive to the skin or seriously damaging to the eye) or  3% (eye irritant), the mixture should be classified accordingly (see also 1.
eye.citation: UN GHS Rev.7 (2017), as adopted by the WHS Regulations, 3.3.3.3.6
